newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Greenspan fright loses punch in Europe.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Greenspan fright loses punch in Europe.

text.p: European bond and stock markets on Friday clawed their way out of the hole caused by fears of an imminent rise in U.S. interest rates but investors had a bumpy ride.
Stock markets on both sides of the Atlantic saw volatile conditions on the back of the expiration of index futures and options contracts in London and the United States.
The Dow Industrials Average bounced up then down in the first few minutes of trade, led lower by a selloff in the shares of Eastman Kodak and tobacco company Philip Morris.

In Europe investors regained some of their nerve after Thursday's turmoil, although interest rate worries continued to dominate after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's hint at an impending rise in U.S. interest rates.

London strategists said the market had probably already taken into account a quarter-point rate rise next week, but the prospect of a British rate rise after the May 1 parliamentary election was likely to continue to weigh on UK shares.
European share markets were helped in part by the dollar, which firmed at first against the mark and yen ahead of next Tuesday's meeting of the Fed's policy-setting open market committee.
The currency later faltered following comments by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky in which she warned Japan against trying to export its way out of recession.
The strength of the dollar was one of the factors cited by Paris traders behind a 1.6 percent rebound in France's blue chip CAC-40 index.
It was a similar story in Frankfurt, where the DAX 30 index closed floor trade up 1.03 percent at 3,298.24. In later computerised trade, the IBIS DAX was up 1.6 percent.
Among Europe's smaller bourses, rises ranged from 2.32 percent in Amsterdam to 1.15 percent in Stockholm and 0.36 in Madrid.
The exception among major stock markets was London, where the FTSE 100 lurched either side of Thursday's depressed close.
The expiry of March index futures and options injected extra volatility into an already jittery cash market and the FTSE 100 index slipped back into the red as Wall Street turned weaker.
"The market has displayed anxiety this week and there is no reason to think that anxiety is going to disappear soon," said Richard Jeffrey, stock maket strategist at Charterhouse Tilney.

Shares in B.A.T Industries recovered from an early tumble after a U.S. legal settlement by tobacco firm Liggett Group Inc sent tobacco shares sliding in the U.S. B.A.T said the settlement would not force it to follow suit.
The stock was up 4.5 p at 493.5 by 1530 GMT.
Traders said a recovery in bond markets on both sides of the Atlantic supported equities.
British and German government bond markets edged higher early on, tracking the overnight rebound in U.S. Treasuries, althoughT-bonds opened later started narrowly weaker.
Next Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) also dominated the foreign exchange market, with Greenspan's comments adding to expectations of a quarter point rate rise .

Greenspan, who has repeatedly spooked the markets in recent months, acknowledged the current benign inflation outlook in the U.S. on Thursday but highlighted the potential for inflationary pressures and reiterated the Fed's pre-emptive stance on monetary policy.

"The comments from Greenspan appear to greenlight a move higher on Tuesday," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank in London. "Greenspan had a clear way to dampen rate hike speculation and he didn't."
By 1530 GMT the dollar was trading at 1.6851 marks and 122.50 yen, down from 1.6916 marks and 123.74 yen in late European trade on Thursday.

"The dollar might not make much headway ahead of the FOMC but it's being buoyed by Greenspan's comments, which weren't as neutral as we expected," said Peter Wood, a currency trader at Bank of Boston in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.6851 marks and 122.50 yen, down from 1.6916 marks and 123.74 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 0.5 points, or 0.01 percent, at 4,257.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 38.54 points, or 1.51 percent, at 2,592.26.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 33.57 points, or 1.03 percent, at 3,298.24. In screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX index was up 42.31 points at 3,289.34.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed firmer at $352.80 versus $351.70 in the morning, while silver was up one cent at $5.19.
